1) the continuous dependence on the initial values is generally not satisfied for impulsive delay systems, and that 2) it can be satisfied for some special impulsive delay systems.
the continuous dependence of solutions of impulsive delay differential equation with respect to initial data is generally not satisfied.

(i) continuous dependence of solutions on the initial values holds in general for impulsive differential equations with finite delays; (ii) the property of continuous time-dependence, however, does not hold in general.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the continuous dependence of solutions of impulsive delay differential systems on initial data.
the study of the continuous dependence of solutions on initial functions, which is a basic property for impulsive delay systems.
the continuous dependence of solutions to impulsive delay differential systems with respect to initial data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

continuous dependence with respect, for example, to initial time, initial functions and initial values is generally not true for impulsive delay systems, but it is true for impulsive systems, and it is true for delay systems.
the impulsive delay differential system does not have continuous dependence on initial values in general.
continuous dependence with respect on initial functions is satisfied for impulsive delay systems, but not with respect to the other initial data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in order to obtain the continuous dependence of solutions on initial values, the initial functions should be continuous, but the initial time can be any point on the interval of definition of the solution.

the solutions of impulsive delay differential systems are not generally continuous with respect to the whole initial data, but they are continuous with respect to initial time, or the initial time interval.

the impulsive effects and the time delay in the system may cause the continuous dependence on initial values to fail, and the impulsive effects may cause the continuous dependences on initial time and initial functions to fail, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
continuous dependence with respect, for example, to the initial time can be restored if one restricts to the set of solutions which satisfy some a priori bounds on the initial data.
the continuous dependence property with respect to the time variable can be restored by imposing some mild additional conditions on the impulsive delay differential equation.
the property of continuous (with respect to time) dependence on initial values can be restored if we consider the solutions of a system of impulsive delay differential inequalities.
